citation: Cordray, D., Pion, G., Brandt, C., Molefe, A., & Toby, M. (2012). The Impact of the Measures of Academic Progress (MAP) Program on Student Reading Achievement. Final Report (NCEE 2013-4000). Washington, DC: National Center for Education Evaluation and Regional Assistance, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education. (Prepared by Regional Educational Laboratory Midwest / Learning Point Associates, an affiliate of the American Institutes for Research.)
design: School-level cluster RCT (block/crossover by district): 32 schools in 5 Illinois districts randomly assigned within district so that each school implemented the MAP program in grade 4 OR grade 5; this yields two parallel experiments. Grade 4 contrast = 16 MAP-in-grade-4 schools vs 16 control (grade-4 classes in the MAP-in-grade-5 schools). Grade 5 contrast = 16 MAP-in-grade-5 schools vs 16 control. Intervention = MAP = NWEA computer-adaptive benchmark testing + teacher TPD (four one-day training sessions + on-site MAP-coach consultative visits + on-demand support to interpret data and differentiate reading instruction). Comparison = business-as-usual (no benchmark/MAP-style assessment or training). Subject = reading/English language arts; grades 4 and 5 (registry grade band 3-6). Impacts estimated via 2-level HLM (students in schools) with district fixed effects, pretest and student/teacher/school covariates; immediate post-intervention wave = end of Year 2 (2009/10). Grade 4 = confirmatory; grade 5 = exploratory.
problems: Subject is READING/ELA (ISAT reading + MAP reading-and-language-usage composite), not math/STEM. The registry/meta-analysis row 19 lists this study under 'TPD for digital tools' and the SYNTHETIC fixture coded it as STEM; the actual report measures reading achievement only, so outcome_subject is set to Reading per the spec mapping (reading/literacy/ELA -> Reading). Flagging the STEM-vs-Reading discrepancy for the central merge. The report calls the standardized impact (impact divided by the control-group SD of the outcome) the 'effect size' (d); I take it directly as the model-based SMD and apply the Hedges J small-sample correction (J ~ 0.9996 at these df, so g essentially equals the reported ES). The report does NOT publish an SE on the standardized ES; I derived g_se = impact_se / control_group_SD, where control_group_SD = impact / reported_ES (verified against the appendix B variance components: e.g. grade-4 ISAT total variance 610.6+58.2 gives SD 25.86 vs implied 25.8). These SEs come from the cluster-adjusted HLM, so cluster_adjusted=true and g_var = g_se^2 already accounts for clustering. The MAP composite is NWEA's own instrument (the intervention's test), labelled researcher_made/developer; the ISAT is the independent state standardized test (the meta-analysis kept only independent measures, but both are extracted and labelled per spec). ICC recorded is the unadjusted (Model 1) design-effect ICC (0.09 grade 4, 0.07 grade 5). Teacher-practice / differentiated-instruction and implementation-fidelity outcomes were skipped (not student achievement). Year 1 (2008/09) waves were interim; Year 2 is the end-of-treatment wave extracted here.

effect_sizes.arm_label: MAP program (NWEA benchmark testing + teacher training/coaching in differentiated reading instruction) vs business-as-usual control -- grade 4 (confirmatory experiment)
effect_sizes.test_name: Illinois Standards Achievement Test (ISAT) reading scale score, spring 2010
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's model-based standardized impact (ES = impact / control-group SD = 1.29 / 25.80 = 0.05) taken as d, standardized by the control-group SD of the ISAT reading score. Hedges J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1) with df = n_t+n_c-2 = 1912 gives J = 0.99961, so g = J*d = 0.0500. g_se = impact_se / control_SD = 1.570/25.80 = 0.0609, times J = 0.0608 (from the cluster-adjusted 2-level HLM); g_var = g_se^2 = 0.0037. Control SD (25.80) reconstructed as impact/ES and cross-checked against Table B.2 Model 1 variance components (sqrt(610.6+58.2)=25.86).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.61 Table 4.1 (ISAT row); detail in Table B.2 (pp.B7-B9)
effect_sizes.notes: Confirmatory headline outcome (chapter 4). Impact 1.29, SE 1.570, p=.412 (not significant); reported ES 0.05. MAP mean 215.6, control 214.3 (regression-adjusted, district-weighted). Overall impact is the district-weighted average of full-model (Model 4) district-specific impacts. n_t/n_c are the analytic samples reported in Table 4.1 (complete eligible sample = 1,914 grade-4 students from 32 schools, multiple imputation for missing data; 85 grade-4 teachers). n_clusters = 16 MAP schools + 16 control schools = 32 (less than 4 schools withdrew immediately after randomization). ISAT = independent state standardized reading test.

effect_sizes.g_method: Report's model-based standardized impact (ES = impact / control-group SD = 0.96 / 13.71 = 0.07) taken as d, standardized by the control-group SD of the MAP composite score. Hedges J with df = 1912 = 0.99961, so g = J*d = 0.0700. g_se = impact_se / control_SD = 0.891/13.71 = 0.0650, times J = 0.0649 (cluster-adjusted HLM); g_var = g_se^2 = 0.004218. Control SD (13.71) reconstructed as impact/ES; Table B.3 Model 1 variance components sqrt(153.4+15.8)=13.01 (RIT-scale SD on the order of 13-15).

effect_sizes.notes: Confirmatory headline outcome (chapter 4), measured on the intervention's own NWEA MAP instrument (reading + language-usage composite), hence test_type researcher_made/developer; the meta-analysis used only independent measures so this row is likely filtered out centrally but extracted per spec. Impact 0.96, SE 0.891, p=.280 (not significant); reported ES 0.07. MAP mean 202.5, control 201.5. Same analytic sample/clusters as the ISAT grade-4 row.

effect_sizes.g_method: Report's model-based standardized impact (ES = impact / control-group SD = -1.48 / 29.60 = -0.05) taken as d, standardized by the control-group SD of the ISAT reading score.
